answer:
I fixed the two commits that broke the build, changing only the source. The full suite now passes: 517 of 517 tests, up from 8 failing.

**1. `958d3ae` "Money: thousands separators in formatMoney"** (`src/money.js`)
While adding comma grouping, this commit also switched the cents padding from `padStart` to `padEnd`. As a result, 1 cent showed as `$0.10` instead of `$0.01`. That broke 4 money tests, the `PIN-03` render row (`$1.50` instead of `$1.05`), and the CA-ON SPRING10 total row. I put `padStart` back and kept the comma grouping.

**2. `4188e9a` "Invoice: per-line discount groundwork"** (`src/invoice.js`)
This commit set `taxable = subtotal`, so tax was charged on the amount before an order code (such as SPRING10) was taken off. Before, tax was charged on `subtotal - discount`, and the commit message says order codes "behave as before". I changed it to `taxable = subtotal - discount`. This fixed the two failing CA-ON SPRING10 invoice tests.

Everything else from those commits is unchanged: comma grouping, line discounts, the `lineDiscounts`/`taxable` fields, the empty-invoice check, and the line-discounts row in the rendered invoice. The other three commits since v2.0.0 didn't cause any failures. The only test edits since the tag were in `test/money.test.js` (updating expected output to include commas) and five new lines in `test/invoice.test.js`. I left all test files as they were.

The fixes are not committed yet.

cat src/money.js src/invoice.js && git show 958d3ae 4188e9a -- src | head -200
git diff --stat v2.0.0 HEAD -- test && git diff v2.0.0 HEAD -- test | grep '^-[^-]' | head -20
